# Call Rust code from R ![rextendr logo](reference/figures/rextendr-logo.png)

The `rextendr` package supports developers who want to build R packages
that call Rust code with [extendr](https://github.com/extendr/extendr).
See the [documentation](https://extendr.rs/) for more details.

## Installation

To install release version from CRAN, run:

``` r
install.packages("rextendr")
```

or use [remotes](https://remotes.r-lib.org)

``` r
remotes::install_cran("rextendr")
```

You can also install [rextendr](https://extendr.rs/rextendr/) from
[r-universe](https://extendr.r-universe.dev/rextendr):

``` r
install.packages(
  "rextendr",
  repos = c("https://extendr.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org")
)
```

Latest development version can be installed from GitHub:

``` r
remotes::install_github("extendr/rextendr")
```

To execute Rust code, you will also need to set up a working Rust
toolchain. See the [installation
guide](https://extendr.rs/get-started.html) for help.

## Usage

``` r
library(rextendr)
```

### Sitrep

A good first step is to check the status of Rust toolchain and available
targets using
[`rust_sitrep()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_sitrep.md).
If everything is OK, you should see something like this:

``` r
rust_sitrep()
# Rust infrastructure sitrep:
# ✔ "rustup": 1.26.0 (5af9b9484 2023-04-05)
# ✔ "cargo": 1.72.0 (103a7ff2e 2023-08-15)
# ℹ host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# ℹ toolchain: stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (default)
# ℹ target: x86_64-pc-windows-gnu
```

If, for instance, no toolchain is found, you will see something like
this:

``` r
rust_sitrep()
# Rust infrastructure sitrep:
# ✔ "rustup": 1.26.0 (5af9b9484 2023-04-05)
# ✔ "cargo": 1.72.0 (103a7ff2e 2023-08-15)
# ℹ host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# ! Toolchain stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc is required to be installed and set as default
# ℹ Run `rustup toolchain install stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` to install it
# ℹ Run `rustup default stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` to make it default
```

Finally, if you are missing the required target (on all platforms but
Windows [rextendr](https://extendr.rs/rextendr/) uses default target),
the report will resemble the following:

``` r
rust_sitrep()
# Rust infrastructure sitrep:
# ✔ "rustup": 1.26.0 (5af9b9484 2023-04-05)
# ✔ "cargo": 1.72.0 (103a7ff2e 2023-08-15)
# ℹ host: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# i toolchains: nightly-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (default)
# i targets: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and i686-pc-windows-msvc
# ! Target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu is required on this host machine
# i Run `rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` to install it
```

### Code examples

Basic use example:

``` r
# create a Rust function
rust_function("fn add(a:f64, b:f64) -> f64 { a + b }")

# call it from R
add(2.5, 4.7)
#> [1] 7.2
```

Something more sophisticated:

``` r
# Rust function that computes a sum of integer or double vectors, preserving the type
rust_function(
  "fn get_sum(x : Either<Integers, Doubles>) -> Either<Rint, Rfloat> {
      match x {
          Either::Left(x) => Either::Left(x.iter().sum()),
          Either::Right(x) => Either::Right(x.iter().sum()),
      }
  }",
  use_dev_extendr = TRUE, # Use development version of extendr from GitHub
  features = "either" # Enable support for Either crate
)

x <- 1:5
y <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)

tibble::tibble(
  Name = c("x", "y"),
  Data = list(x, y),
  Types = purrr::map_chr(Data, typeof),
  Sum = purrr::map(Data, get_sum),
  SumRaw = purrr::flatten_dbl(Sum),
  ResultType = purrr::map_chr(Sum, typeof)
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   Name  Data      Types   Sum       SumRaw ResultType
#>   <chr> <list>    <chr>   <list>     <dbl> <chr>     
#> 1 x     <int [5]> integer <int [1]>     15 integer   
#> 2 y     <dbl [5]> double  <dbl [1]>     15 double
```

The package also enables a new chunk type for knitr, `extendr`, which
compiles and evaluates Rust code. For example, a code chunk such as this
one:

```` markdown
```{extendr}
rprintln!("Hello from Rust!");

let x = 5;
let y = 7;
let z = x*y;

z
```
````

would create the following output in the knitted document:

``` rust
rprintln!("Hello from Rust!");

let x = 5;
let y = 7;
let z = x*y;

z
#> Hello from Rust!
#> [1] 35
```

### Project scaffolding

To setup a project with extendr scaffolding, first initialize an R
package directory with
[`usethis::create_package()`](https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/create_package.html).
Then navigate to that directory and call
[`rextendr::use_extendr()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_extendr.md).

``` r
usethis::create_package("helloextendr")

rextendr::use_extendr()
# ✔ Setting active project to "./helloextendr".
# ℹ First time using rextendr. Upgrading automatically...
# ℹ Setting `Config/rextendr/version` to "0.5.0" in the DESCRIPTION file.
# ℹ Setting `SystemRequirements` to "Cargo (Rust's package manager), rustc >= 1.65.0, xz" in the DESCRIPTION file.
# ✔ Creating src/rust/src.
# ✔ Writing src/entrypoint.c.
# ✔ Writing src/Makevars.in.
# ✔ Writing src/Makevars.win.in.
# ✔ Writing cleanup.
# ✔ Writing cleanup.win.
# ✔ Writing src/.gitignore.
# ✔ Writing src/rust/Cargo.toml.
# ✔ Writing src/rust/src/lib.rs.
# ✔ Writing src/hellowworld-win.def.
# ✔ Writing R/extendr-wrappers.R
# ✔ Writing tools/document.R.
# ✔ Writing tools/msrv.R.
# ✔ Writing tools/config.R.
# ✔ Writing configure.
# ✔ Writing configure.win.
# ✔ Adding "^\\.vscode$" to .Rbuildignore.
# ✔ Writing .vscode/settings.json.
# ✔ Adding R to Depends field in DESCRIPTION.
# ✔ Adding "^src/\\.cargo$" to .Rbuildignore.
# ✔ Adding "^src/rust/vendor$" to .Rbuildignore.
# ✔ Adding "src/rust/vendor" to .gitignore.
# ✔ Adding "^src/rust/target$" to .Rbuildignore.
# ✔ Adding "^src/Makevars$" to .Rbuildignore.
# ✔ Adding "src/Makevars" to .gitignore.
# ✔ Adding "^src/Makevars\\.win$" to .Rbuildignore.
# ✔ Adding "src/Makevars.win" to .gitignore.
# ✔ Finished configuring extendr for package hellowworld.
# • Please run `devtools::document()` for changes to take effect.
# ℹ Call `use_extendr_badge()` to add an extendr badge to your README
```

The output is pretty lengthy, showing all the scaffolding files that are
generated, along with the initiated Rust project in `src/rust/`. Some of
this may change as we update and improve extendr tools, but the main
thing to note here is that
[`devtools::document()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/document.html)
is sufficient to compile the hello-world example that `lib.rs` contains
by default, generate the necessary wrappers, and build the R package.
Then
[`devtools::load_all()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/load_all.html)
will make them available in your current R session.

``` r
devtools::document()
devtools::load_all()

hello("world")
# [1] "Hello world!"
```

# Package index

## Compiling and running Rust code

- [`rust_source()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_source.md)
  [`rust_function()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_source.md)
  [`extendr_options()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_source.md)
  [`print(`*`<extendr_opts>`*`)`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_source.md)
  : Compile Rust code and call from R
- [`rust_eval()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_eval.md)
  : Evaluate Rust code
- [`eng_extendr()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/eng_extendr.md)
  [`eng_extendrsrc()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/eng_extendr.md)
  : Knitr engines

## Package development

- [`use_extendr()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_extendr.md)
  : Set up a package for use with Rust extendr code
- [`use_crate()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_crate.md)
  : Add dependencies to a Cargo.toml manifest file
- [`document()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/document.md)
  **\[deprecated\]** : Compile Rust code and generate package
  documentation.
- [`register_extendr()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/register_extendr.md)
  **\[deprecated\]** : Register the extendr module of a package with R
- [`write_license_note()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/write_license_note.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Generate LICENSE.note file.
- [`clean()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/clean.md) :
  Clean Rust binaries and package cache.
- [`cran`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/cran.md) : CRAN
  compliant extendr packages
- [`vendor_crates()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/vendor_crates.md)
  [`vendor_pkgs()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/vendor_crates.md)
  **\[deprecated\]** : Vendor Rust dependencies
- [`use_msrv()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_msrv.md)
  : Set the minimum supported rust version (MSRV)
- [`use_vscode()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_vscode.md)
  [`use_positron()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_vscode.md)
  : Set up VS Code configuration for an rextendr project

## Various utility functions

- [`to_toml()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/to_toml.md)
  :

  Convert R [`list()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/list.html) into
  toml-compatible format.

- [`make_module_macro()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/make_module_macro.md)
  : Generate extendr module macro for Rust source

- [`rust_sitrep()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/rust_sitrep.md)
  : Report on Rust infrastructure

- [`read_cargo_metadata()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/read_cargo_metadata.md)
  : Retrieve metadata for packages and workspaces

- [`use_extendr_badge()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/use_extendr_badge.md)
  : extendr README badge

- [`update_scaffold()`](https://extendr.github.io/rextendr/reference/update_scaffold.md)
  : Update extendr scaffolding
